question: Which ministry launched the Swavalambini initiative in March 2025 to promote women entrepreneurship in India?

options.text: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Swavalambini initiative** was launched in **March 2025** by the **Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship** to promote **women entrepreneurship** across India.
 
• The initiative focuses on empowering women by providing access to **skill development programs**, mentorship, and financial support to enhance their participation in entrepreneurial activities.
 
• It aims to create an enabling ecosystem for women entrepreneurs through partnerships with **financial institutions, industry bodies, and non-governmental organizations (NGOs)**.
 
• The program emphasizes **capacity building** among women through specialized courses, workshops, and training programs tailored to their needs.
 
• Under this initiative, the government seeks to address barriers such as **lack of access to credit, technology, and market linkages**, which have historically limited women's entrepreneurial potential.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship:**

 
 
• Established in **2014**, this ministry is responsible for coordinating skill development efforts across India.
 
• It oversees initiatives like the **Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)**, which aims to provide short-term skill training to youth.
 
• The ministry collaborates with industry leaders to align skill development programs with market needs and to promote entrepreneurship.
 
• It aims to bridge the gap between workforce requirements and skill availability through focused programs and policies.
 
 
 
• **Women Entrepreneurship in India:**
 
 
• Women entrepreneurs account for approximately **14% of total entrepreneurs** in India, according to government data.
 
• They face challenges such as **limited access to funding, societal norms, and inadequate networking opportunities**.
 
• Government initiatives like **Stand-Up India** and **Mahila E-Haat** aim to support women entrepreneurs by providing funding and market access.
 
• Promoting women entrepreneurship is critical for achieving **inclusive economic growth** and gender equality in the workforce.
 
 
 
• **Skill Development Programs for Women:**
 
 
• Various programs have been launched to enhance women’s skills, such as the **National Skill Development Mission** and **Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana**.
 
• These programs emphasize **hands-on training, digital literacy, and sector-specific skills**, such as textiles, handicrafts, and IT services.
 
• Special focus is given to rural women to boost their participation in economic activities through self-employment opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact of Women Entrepreneurs:**
 
 
• Encouraging women in entrepreneurship contributes significantly to **GDP growth** and employment generation.
 
• Studies indicate that closing the gender gap in entrepreneurship could increase India's GDP by **27%**.
 
• Women entrepreneurs bring diverse perspectives and innovative approaches to business, fostering **economic resilience and sustainability**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Stand-Up India Scheme:**

 
 
• Launched in **2016**, this scheme provides loans ranging from **₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore** for women and SC/ST entrepreneurs.
 
• It aims to promote entrepreneurship by facilitating access to bank loans for greenfield projects.
 
 
 
• **Mahila E-Haat:**
 
 
• An online marketing platform launched by the **Ministry of Women and Child Development** to support women entrepreneurs.
 
• It showcases products made by women to enable direct consumer purchase, enhancing their market reach.
 
 
 
• **MUDRA Scheme:**
 
 
• This scheme provides financial assistance to micro and small enterprises, including women-led businesses.
 
• It offers loans under three categories: **Shishu, Kishore, and Tarun**, depending on the funding needs.
 
 
 
• **National Policy for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship:**
 
 
• Introduced in **2015**, this policy emphasizes the development of entrepreneurial skills and fostering innovation.
 
• It encourages women’s participation in skill development programs and entrepreneurial ventures.
